To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the rapid metabolic actions of DEX in ob/ob but not lean mice are due to an enhancement of hypothalamic NPY secretion.

DEX increases hypothalamic NPY secretion in a phenotype-specific fashion in ob/ob but not lean mice and that DEX-induced hypothalamic NYP secretion is responsible for the rapid suppression of brown adipose tissue activity and increase in plasma insulin concentrations that occur in ob/ob, but not in lean, ADX mice.
DEX acts in a phenotype-specific way to increase NPY secretion from the hypothalamus within 30 min of intracerebro- ventricular injection in ADX ob/ ob mice but not in lean mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the rapid actions of DEX on NPY secretion in the hypothalamo-pituitary axis.
the mechanisms of action of the glucocorticoid DEX in the brain of ob/ob and ob/+ mice.
the mechanisms by which glucocorticoids act in the brain to regulate metabolism in the ob/ob mouse.

DEX ex-erts rapid metabolic actions in ob mice via a phenotype- specific enhancement of NPY release within the central nervous sys-tem, which is mediated by the type II glucocorti-coid receptor.

dexamethasones (DEX) rapid actions in the hypothalamuses of ADX obob mice are mediated by the release of NPY.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DEX exes a rapid phenotype-specific enhancement of hypothalamic NPY secretion that may be a key factor for the rapid onset of the metabolic actions of DEX in ob/ob but not lean mice.

DEX acts in a phenotype-specific way in ob/ob but not lean ADX mice to rapidly increase NPY secretion within specific regions of the hypothalamus, which in turn evokes the rapid-onset metabolic responses observed in these mice.
DEX rapidly evokes a phenotype-specific enhancement in NPY release from hypothalamic arcuate neurons of ADX ob mice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
glucocorticoids can rapidly alter the activity of hypothalamic neurons in a phenotype-specific and region-specific manner.
DEX rapidly increases hypothal-amus neuropeptide Y release in adrenalect-omized obese mice.
DEX can act within the central nervous systems of ob/ob and other metabolic disease models to rapidly evoke metabolic changes by increasing the release of NPY.
